## DOM mismatches

### HP1001

**Text differs between server and client** · `text-mismatch` · default severity: error

The server HTML contains different text than the browser rendered during hydration.

How to fix:

- Render exactly the same text on the server and in the first client render.
- Move browser-only or time-dependent values into useEffect, or compute them on the server and pass them down as props.

Online: https://hydration.jscrate.dev/docs/issues/hp1001

### HP1002

**Attribute differs between server and client** · `attribute-mismatch` · default severity: error

An attribute value in the server HTML differs from the value React rendered on the client. React does not patch attributes during hydration.

How to fix:

- Compute the attribute from data that is identical on the server and the client.
- React does not fix attributes during hydration, so users keep seeing the server value until the next update.

Online: https://hydration.jscrate.dev/docs/issues/hp1002

### HP1003

**Inline style differs between server and client** · `style-mismatch` · default severity: error

The style attribute rendered on the server differs from the style React applies on the client.

How to fix:

- Make inline styles depend only on data available on both server and client, or apply them after mount.

Online: https://hydration.jscrate.dev/docs/issues/hp1003

### HP1004

**Class name differs between server and client** · `class-mismatch` · default severity: error

The class attribute rendered on the server differs from the className React renders on the client. The page keeps the server classes.

How to fix:

- Make class names deterministic between server and client.
- For themes, read the preference on the server (for example from a cookie) or set the class with a pre-hydration script and suppressHydrationWarning on that element.
- For CSS-in-JS, set up the library's server style registry so class names are generated in the same order.

Online: https://hydration.jscrate.dev/docs/issues/hp1004

### HP1005

**Attribute only present in the server HTML** · `extra-attribute` · default severity: warning

The server HTML has an attribute that React does not render on the client.

How to fix:

- Remove the attribute from the server output or render it on the client too.

Online: https://hydration.jscrate.dev/docs/issues/hp1005

### HP1006

**Attribute missing from the server HTML** · `missing-attribute` · default severity: error

React renders an attribute on the client that the server HTML does not have.

How to fix:

- Render the attribute on the server as well, or add it after mount in useEffect.

Online: https://hydration.jscrate.dev/docs/issues/hp1006

### HP1007

**Different element rendered on server and client** · `element-mismatch` · default severity: error

The server rendered one element and the client rendered a different one in the same place.

How to fix:

- Render the same element type on server and client; branch on data that both sides share.

Online: https://hydration.jscrate.dev/docs/issues/hp1007

### HP1008

**Element only present in the server HTML** · `extra-element` · default severity: error

The server HTML contains a node the client render does not produce.

How to fix:

- Do not render server-only nodes inside hydrated components; use the same condition on both sides.

Online: https://hydration.jscrate.dev/docs/issues/hp1008

### HP1009

**Element missing from the server HTML** · `missing-element` · default severity: error

The client render produces a node the server HTML does not contain.

How to fix:

- Render client-only nodes after mount (useEffect) or with a client-only component.

Online: https://hydration.jscrate.dev/docs/issues/hp1009

### HP1010

**React discarded server HTML and rendered a branch again** · `branch-replaced` · default severity: error

Hydration failed inside this branch, so React threw away the server HTML and rendered it on the client. This costs performance and resets state.

How to fix:

- Fix the mismatch inside this branch; React re-renders it on every page load until then.

Online: https://hydration.jscrate.dev/docs/issues/hp1010

### HP1011

**React discarded the whole server-rendered page** · `root-replaced` · default severity: error

Hydration failed outside any Suspense boundary, so React re-rendered the entire root on the client.

How to fix:

- Fix the mismatch or wrap the unstable part in a Suspense boundary so React only re-renders that part.

Online: https://hydration.jscrate.dev/docs/issues/hp1011

### HP1012

**Form state differs between server and client** · `form-state-mismatch` · default severity: warning

A form control value, checked or selected state changed during hydration.

How to fix:

- Use defaultValue/defaultChecked with values that are identical on server and client.

Online: https://hydration.jscrate.dev/docs/issues/hp1012

### HP1013

**dangerouslySetInnerHTML differs between server and client** · `inner-html-mismatch` · default severity: error

The HTML injected with dangerouslySetInnerHTML differs between the server and the client. React does not patch it.

How to fix:

- Make the injected HTML identical on server and client, or render it after mount.

Online: https://hydration.jscrate.dev/docs/issues/hp1013

### HP1014

**Document head differs between server and client** · `head-mismatch` · default severity: warning

Metadata, stylesheets or scripts in <head> changed during hydration.

Online: https://hydration.jscrate.dev/docs/issues/hp1014

### HP1015

**Whitespace differs between server and client** · `whitespace-mismatch` · default severity: error

Only whitespace differs, which usually means something rewrote the HTML between the server and the browser.

How to fix:

- Turn off HTML minification that removes whitespace (for example CDN "Auto Minify") for server-rendered React pages.
- Avoid relying on whitespace-only text nodes between elements.

Online: https://hydration.jscrate.dev/docs/issues/hp1015

## Problems React reported

### HP2001

**React reported a hydration error** · `react-hydration-error` · default severity: error

React reported that hydration failed. The DOM comparison could not locate the exact difference.

How to fix:

- Run hydration-proof in development mode (--mode dev) for React's detailed diff.

Online: https://hydration.jscrate.dev/docs/issues/hp2001

### HP2002

**React warned about a hydration mismatch** · `react-hydration-warning` · default severity: warning

React logged a hydration mismatch warning (development builds only).

Online: https://hydration.jscrate.dev/docs/issues/hp2002

### HP2003

**A Suspense boundary switched to client rendering** · `boundary-client-rendered` · default severity: error

React could not hydrate a Suspense boundary and rendered it on the client instead.

How to fix:

- Check the error React reported for this boundary; the boundary is rendered on the client until it is fixed.

Online: https://hydration.jscrate.dev/docs/issues/hp2003

### HP2004

**The root switched to client rendering** · `root-client-rendered` · default severity: error

An error during hydration outside any Suspense boundary made React render the whole root on the client.

How to fix:

- Wrap unstable parts in Suspense boundaries so a hydration error does not re-render the whole page.

Online: https://hydration.jscrate.dev/docs/issues/hp2004

### HP2005

**An update arrived before hydration finished** · `update-before-hydration` · default severity: warning

A Suspense boundary or root received an update before it finished hydrating (React errors 421/424).

How to fix:

- Wrap updates triggered during hydration in startTransition.

Online: https://hydration.jscrate.dev/docs/issues/hp2005

### HP2006

**The server could not finish rendering a boundary** · `server-render-error` · default severity: error

The server failed to render part of the page and the client had to render it (React error 419).

How to fix:

- Check the server logs: the server threw while rendering this Suspense boundary.

Online: https://hydration.jscrate.dev/docs/issues/hp2006

### HP2007

**Uncaught error while loading the page** · `page-error` · default severity: warning

A script threw during page load. It may or may not be related to hydration.

Online: https://hydration.jscrate.dev/docs/issues/hp2007

## Markup the browser repaired

### HP3001

**Invalid HTML nesting** · `invalid-nesting` · default severity: error

The markup nests elements in a way HTML does not allow. Browsers repair it while parsing, so the DOM no longer matches what React rendered.

How to fix:

- Fix the nesting: for example use <span> instead of <div> inside <p>, and wrap table rows in <tbody>.
- The browser rewrites invalid markup before React hydrates, so the DOM never matches what React rendered.

Online: https://hydration.jscrate.dev/docs/issues/hp3001

### HP3002

**Interactive element nested in another** · `nested-interactive` · default severity: error

Links, buttons and forms cannot contain another element of the same kind.

How to fix:

- Do not nest links inside links, buttons inside buttons or forms inside forms.

Online: https://hydration.jscrate.dev/docs/issues/hp3002

### HP3003

**Duplicate id attribute** · `duplicate-id` · default severity: info

Several elements share the same id.

Online: https://hydration.jscrate.dev/docs/issues/hp3003

## Changes made outside React

### HP4001

**The page was modified before React hydrated** · `pre-hydration-mutation` · default severity: error

A script, browser extension or third-party tag changed the server-rendered DOM before hydration.

How to fix:

- Find the script that changes the DOM before hydration and run it after hydration, or make it change only elements outside React's tree.
- If a browser extension causes this, it cannot be fixed in code; add an ignore rule for the extension's attributes.

Online: https://hydration.jscrate.dev/docs/issues/hp4001

### HP4002

**A browser extension changed the page** · `extension-mutation` · default severity: info

Changes typical of browser extensions (grammar checkers, password managers, translators) were found.

How to fix:

- This comes from a browser extension on the test machine or simulated by your scenario; ignore it if it is expected.

Online: https://hydration.jscrate.dev/docs/issues/hp4002

### HP4003

**HTML was rewritten between the server and the browser** · `html-rewritten` · default severity: error

The HTML the browser received differs from what the origin server produced (CDN minification, proxies, edge functions).

How to fix:

- Disable HTML rewriting (minification, email obfuscation, injection) for server-rendered pages at the CDN or proxy.

Online: https://hydration.jscrate.dev/docs/issues/hp4003

## Interaction during hydration

### HP5001

**An interaction before hydration was lost** · `lost-interaction` · default severity: error

A click or input made before hydration finished had no effect.

Online: https://hydration.jscrate.dev/docs/issues/hp5001

### HP5002

**User input was reset during hydration** · `input-reset` · default severity: error

Text typed before hydration finished was cleared or replaced.

Online: https://hydration.jscrate.dev/docs/issues/hp5002

### HP5003

**Focus was lost during hydration** · `focus-lost` · default severity: warning

The focused element was replaced during hydration.

Online: https://hydration.jscrate.dev/docs/issues/hp5003

## suppressHydrationWarning audit

### HP6001

**Mismatch hidden by suppressHydrationWarning** · `suppressed-mismatch` · default severity: info

The server and client values differ on an element marked with suppressHydrationWarning. React keeps the server value.

How to fix:

- This is fine if the difference is intentional (timestamps, for example). Keep suppressHydrationWarning on the smallest element possible.

Online: https://hydration.jscrate.dev/docs/issues/hp6001

### HP6002

**suppressHydrationWarning cannot hide a structural difference** · `suppression-hides-structure` · default severity: error

suppressHydrationWarning only covers text and attributes one level deep; the elements inside still differ.

How to fix:

- suppressHydrationWarning only covers the element's own text and attributes; fix the structural difference.

Online: https://hydration.jscrate.dev/docs/issues/hp6002

### HP6003

**suppressHydrationWarning with nothing to suppress** · `suppression-unused` · default severity: info

The element is marked with suppressHydrationWarning but its server and client output are identical.

How to fix:

- Remove suppressHydrationWarning if nothing on this element differs, so real mismatches are not hidden later.

Online: https://hydration.jscrate.dev/docs/issues/hp6003

## Test run problems

### HP9001

**Hydration did not finish in time** · `hydration-timeout` · default severity: error

React was on the page but hydration did not complete before the timeout.

How to fix:

- Increase the hydration timeout, or check for Suspense boundaries that never resolve in the test environment.

Online: https://hydration.jscrate.dev/docs/issues/hp9001

### HP9002

**No React found on the page** · `no-react` · default severity: warning

The page loaded without any React renderer, so nothing was hydrated.

How to fix:

- Check that the URL serves a React page and that its scripts load in the test browser.

Online: https://hydration.jscrate.dev/docs/issues/hp9002

### HP9003

**The page is rendered on the client only** · `client-rendered-page` · default severity: info

React mounted with createRoot instead of hydrating server HTML.

Online: https://hydration.jscrate.dev/docs/issues/hp9003

### HP9004

**The page could not be loaded** · `navigation-failed` · default severity: error

The browser could not navigate to the URL.

How to fix:

- Check that the server is running and the URL is correct.

Online: https://hydration.jscrate.dev/docs/issues/hp9004

### HP9005

**The server answered with an error status** · `http-error` · default severity: error

The document response had an HTTP error status.

How to fix:

- Make the route return a success status, or list the status in the route's expected statuses.

Online: https://hydration.jscrate.dev/docs/issues/hp9005

### HP9006

**The server HTML could not be captured** · `body-unavailable` · default severity: warning

The document body was not available, so server-side stages could not be compared.

Online: https://hydration.jscrate.dev/docs/issues/hp9006

### HP9007

**Some capture data was dropped** · `capture-truncated` · default severity: warning

Buffers overflowed while capturing; results may be incomplete.

Online: https://hydration.jscrate.dev/docs/issues/hp9007

### HP9008

**React loaded but never mounted a root** · `no-root` · default severity: warning

A React renderer was injected but no root was created before the timeout.

Online: https://hydration.jscrate.dev/docs/issues/hp9008

### HP9009

**The page never became quiet** · `ready-timeout` · default severity: warning

The ready conditions (quiet DOM, selector, function) were not met before the timeout.

How to fix:

- Increase ready.quietMs/timeout or provide ready.selector for pages with continuous updates.

Online: https://hydration.jscrate.dev/docs/issues/hp9009
